views.name: hero_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  superhero_name,
  full_name,
  gender_id,
  eye_colour_id,
  hair_colour_id,
  skin_colour_id,
  race_id,
  publisher_id,
  alignment_id,
  height_cm,
  weight_kg
FROM superhero

params.description: A normalized one-row-per-hero base view providing identity and core physical/demographic attributes for each superhero.
params.when_to_use: Look up a hero's canonical identifiers, names, and core attributes (height, weight, gender, race, publisher, alignment). | As the base table to join onto when composing downstream aggregations of powers, attributes, or demographics while preserving one-row-per-hero cardinality. | Filtering or selecting heroes by attribute values (e.g., publisher_id, gender_id, height_cm range) before joining to aggregated/detail tables.
params.output_schema: id: surrogate primary key for the hero — derives directly from superhero.id | superhero_name: public/hero alias — derives directly from superhero.superhero_name | full_name: real/secret identity name — derives directly from superhero.full_name | gender_id: foreign key reference to a gender dimension — derives directly from superhero.gender_id | eye_colour_id: foreign key reference to an eye colour dimension — derives directly from superhero.eye_colour_id | hair_colour_id: foreign key reference to a hair colour dimension — derives directly from superhero.hair_colour_id | skin_colour_id: foreign key reference to a skin colour dimension — derives directly from superhero.skin_colour_id | race_id: foreign key reference to a race/ancestry dimension — derives directly from superhero.race_id | publisher_id: foreign key reference to publisher (company) — derives directly from superhero.publisher_id | alignment_id: foreign key reference to alignment (hero/villain/neutral) — derives directly from superhero.alignment_id | height_cm: numerical height in centimetres — derives directly from superhero.height_cm | weight_kg: numerical weight in kilograms — derives directly from superhero.weight_kg
params.grounded_columns: superhero.id | superhero.superhero_name | superhero.full_name | superhero.gender_id | superhero.eye_colour_id | superhero.hair_colour_id | superhero.skin_colour_id | superhero.race_id | superhero.publisher_id | superhero.alignment_id | superhero.height_cm | superhero.weight_kg
params.metric: No aggregated metrics are defined in this normalized base view. All columns are pass-through base columns from superhero table (no SUM/COUNT/AVG etc.).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension/look-up views/tables (one-row-per-dimension-value) on their id keys — safe because hero_base is strictly one-row-per-hero and these dims are one-row-per-key, so measures from hero_base are not duplicated. Examples: join to gender_dim on hero_base.gender_id = gender_dim.id, to publisher_dim on hero_base.publisher_id = publisher_dim.id, to alignment_dim on hero_base.alignment_id. | SAFE: join to hero_demographics (JOIN) on hero_base.id = hero_demographics.id — safe when hero_demographics is one-row-per-hero (it is a join sibling intended to preserve hero row cardinality). | NOT SAFE without aggregation: do NOT directly join hero_base to one-to-many/detail views/tables such as hero_power_assignments (JOIN) or any raw power assignment table that lists multiple powers per hero, because those one-to-many joins will multiply hero_base rows and thereby duplicate any measures or attributes if the downstream logic assumes one-row-per-hero. Instead, either: | - join to an aggregated sibling view (e.g., hero_power_counts or hero_attribute_summary) that provides one-row-per-hero aggregates, or | - aggregate the one-to-many side first (e.g., GROUP BY hero_id) to a single row per hero and then join, or | - use lateral/exists or windowed/array-aggregation patterns that preserve hero cardinality depending on DB capabilities. | When composing metrics that combine hero_base numeric attributes (height_cm, weight_kg) with aggregated counts or sums from other tables, always ensure the other side is pre-aggregated to one row per hero (e.g., hero_power_counts) before joining to avoid incorrect multiplication. | If you need to produce hero-level rows with repeated power rows (one row per hero-power), intentionally join hero_base to hero_power_assignments but treat resulting power-level measures as power-row measures (do not sum height_cm/weight_kg across that join unless dividing/aggregating back to hero-level).

views.description: Normalized one-row-per-hero projection including core descriptive columns and physical measures. Use this as the canonical superhero row for joins and downstream analytics. | Use for: List heroes with their basic attributes; Filter heroes by publisher/gender/alignment/race; Compute aggregates (avg height/weight) per demographic group

views.name: hero_demographics
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.id,
  s.superhero_name,
  s.full_name,
  s.gender_id,
  gender.gender AS gender,
  s.eye_colour_id,
  ec.colour AS eye_colour,
  s.hair_colour_id,
  hc.colour AS hair_colour,
  s.skin_colour_id,
  sc.colour AS skin_colour,
  s.race_id,
  race.race AS race,
  s.publisher_id,
  publisher.publisher_name AS publisher_name,
  s.alignment_id,
  alignment.alignment AS alignment,
  s.height_cm,
  s.weight_kg
FROM superhero AS s
LEFT JOIN gender ON s.gender_id = gender.id
LEFT JOIN colour AS ec ON s.eye_colour_id = ec.id
LEFT JOIN colour AS hc ON s.hair_colour_id = hc.id
LEFT JOIN colour AS sc ON s.skin_colour_id = sc.id
LEFT JOIN race ON s.race_id = race.id
LEFT JOIN publisher ON s.publisher_id = publisher.id
LEFT JOIN alignment ON s.alignment_id = alignment.id

params.description: Provides one-row-per-superhero demographic details (name, identity, categorical attributes, publisher, alignment, and physical measurements).
params.when_to_use: Retrieve demographic attributes for individual superheroes (lookup by id or name). | Join superhero demographics as a dimension when building aggregates about powers, appearances, or events (as long as joins are cardinality-safe). | Filter or group analyses by demographic categories (gender, race, publisher, alignment, colours) and physical measurements (height, weight). | Compose higher-level aggregates that count or summarize heroes by demographic attributes (must aggregate after joining one-to-many facts).
params.output_schema: id: unique identifier of the superhero — derives from superhero.id | superhero_name: public/hero alias — derives from superhero.superhero_name | full_name: civilian/real name — derives from superhero.full_name | gender_id: foreign key id for gender — derives from superhero.gender_id | gender: gender label (human-readable) — derives from gender.gender (joined via gender.id = superhero.gender_id) | eye_colour_id: foreign key id for eye colour — derives from superhero.eye_colour_id | eye_colour: eye colour label — derives from colour.colour (joined via colour.id = superhero.eye_colour_id) | hair_colour_id: foreign key id for hair colour — derives from superhero.hair_colour_id | hair_colour: hair colour label — derives from colour.colour (joined via colour.id = superhero.hair_colour_id) | skin_colour_id: foreign key id for skin colour — derives from superhero.skin_colour_id | skin_colour: skin colour label — derives from colour.colour (joined via colour.id = superhero.skin_colour_id) | race_id: foreign key id for race — derives from superhero.race_id | race: race label — derives from race.race (joined via race.id = superhero.race_id) | publisher_id: foreign key id for publisher — derives from superhero.publisher_id | publisher_name: publisher label — derives from publisher.publisher_name (joined via publisher.id = superhero.publisher_id) | alignment_id: foreign key id for alignment — derives from superhero.alignment_id | alignment: alignment label (e.g., good/evil/neutral) — derives from alignment.alignment (joined via alignment.id = superhero.alignment_id) | height_cm: measured height in centimetres — derives from superhero.height_cm | weight_kg: measured weight in kilograms — derives from superhero.weight_kg
params.grounded_columns: superhero.id | superhero.superhero_name | superhero.full_name | superhero.gender_id | gender.id | gender.gender | superhero.eye_colour_id | colour.id | colour.colour | superhero.hair_colour_id | superhero.skin_colour_id | superhero.race_id | race.id | race.race | superhero.publisher_id | publisher.id | publisher.publisher_name | superhero.alignment_id | alignment.id | alignment.alignment | superhero.height_cm | superhero.weight_kg
params.metric: No aggregated metrics are produced by this view; all output columns are direct base columns or dimension labels. (E.g., height_cm = superhero.height_cm, weight_kg = superhero.weight_kg)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to hero_base (or the underlying superhero table) on id — safe because hero_demographics is one-row-per-superhero (PRIMARY KEY: id) so hero-level measures are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to small lookup/dimension tables (gender, colour, race, publisher, alignment) on their id keys — safe because these were left-joined in the view and are one-row-per-id. | do NOT join hero_demographics directly to any one-to-many tables or views (for example: hero_power_assignments, hero_power_counts, hero_attribute_values, hero_attribute_summary, heroes_with_attributes_and_powers) without handling multiplicity. Those are one-to-many relative to hero and will multiply hero rows and any hero-level measures if joined naively. | If you need aggregated results combining demographics with one-to-many facts (powers, attributes), either: (a) aggregate the one-to-many side first to one-row-per-hero (e.g., use hero_power_counts or hero_attribute_summary) and then join to hero_demographics on id, or (b) join and then re-aggregate and use appropriate DISTINCT/COUNT(DISTINCT ...) or SUM over measures to remove duplication. Example safe pattern: SELECT d.publisher_name, COUNT(*) FROM hero_demographics d JOIN hero_power_counts pc ON d.id = pc.hero_id GROUP BY d.publisher_name — only safe because pc is pre-aggregated per hero. | When composing higher-level measures (counts, averages) from hero_demographics, compute aggregations at the query layer (e.g., AVG(height_cm) GROUP BY alignment) — no internal aggregations in this view to worry about. | Avoid joining multiple different one-to-many views at once to hero_demographics unless each has been reduced to one row per hero or you use a multi-stage aggregation to prevent Cartesian multiplication.

views.description: Denormalized hero rows enriched with human-readable dimension labels (gender, colours, race, publisher, alignment). Useful when presenting hero attributes or grouping by these labels. | Use for: Show hero names with readable demographics and publisher; Group heroes by publisher, alignment, race, or colour; Filter heroes by human-readable attributes (e.g., alignment = 'Good')
validated_on: Which publisher published the slowest superhero?
Give the publisher ID of Star Trek.
What is the total number of superheroes without full name?

views.name: hero_attribute_values
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ha.hero_id,
  ha.attribute_id,
  attribute.attribute_name AS attribute_name,
  ha.attribute_value
FROM hero_attribute AS ha
LEFT JOIN attribute ON ha.attribute_id = attribute.id

params.description: Provides one row per hero-attribute pair showing the attribute id, attribute name, and that hero's stored attribute value.
params.when_to_use: Look up the value of a specific attribute for one or many heroes (e.g., 'what is hero 42's strength?'). | List all attributes and values for a given hero (e.g., 'show attributes for hero 123'). | Compose higher-level aggregations by starting from per-hero-per-attribute values (e.g., average attribute_value per attribute). | Join hero attribute values into reports that include hero or attribute metadata while preserving the per-hero-per-attribute grain.
params.output_schema: hero_id: the hero identifier — derived directly from hero_attribute.hero_id | attribute_id: the attribute identifier — derived directly from hero_attribute.attribute_id | attribute_name: the human-readable name of the attribute — derived from attribute.attribute_name (via LEFT JOIN on attribute.id = hero_attribute.attribute_id) | attribute_value: the stored value for this hero's attribute — derived directly from hero_attribute.attribute_value
params.metric: attribute_value = hero_attribute.attribute_value (base column; no aggregation in this view) | this view is at grain (hero_id, attribute_id) so any aggregate metric must be defined by aggregating attribute_value (for example: avg_attribute_value = AVG(attribute_value) GROUP BY attribute_id)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to hero_base (NORM) on hero_id — safe because hero_base is one-row-per-hero, so joining will not duplicate this view's hero-attribute rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to attribute (dimension) on attribute_id — safe because attribute is one-row-per-attribute (the view already LEFT JOINs attribute for attribute_name), so joining will not duplicate rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to hero_demographics (JOIN) on hero_id — safe if hero_demographics is one-row-per-hero; it will not duplicate hero-attribute rows. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views such as hero_power_assignments (JOIN) or heroes_with_attributes_and_powers (JOIN) without re-aggregation or careful deduplication — those are one-to-many from hero (or hero-attribute) and will multiply rows and thus duplicate attribute_value measures. | if you need to combine attribute_value with measures from hero_power_assignments or similar one-to-many sources, first aggregate the one-to-many source to the (hero_id) or (hero_id, attribute_id) grain as appropriate (for example: COUNT or SUM per hero_id) before joining to this view to avoid inflating attribute_value-derived aggregates. | when composing aggregates: to compute attribute-level metrics (e.g., average attribute_value per attribute_id) aggregate attribute_value over this view and do not join to any child (many-side) detail before aggregating. | when joining ranked or aggregated sibling views (hero_power_counts, hero_attribute_summary, hero_power_rank): ensure those sibling views are at a compatible grain (hero_id or hero_id+attribute_id). Join on matching keys only; joining to a view that is aggregated to a coarser grain (e.g., per-hero) is safe but will change result cardinality and may require GROUP BY to preserve intended measures.

views.description: One row per (hero_id, attribute_id) with the attribute name and value. Use for aggregations across attributes or to pivot attributes per hero. | Use for: Find heroes' values for a given attribute (e.g., Intelligence); Compute average attribute_value by attribute_name or by hero; Pivot attributes to have one row per hero with multiple attribute columns

views.name: hero_power_assignments
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  hp.hero_id,
  hp.power_id,
  superpower.power_name AS power_name
FROM hero_power AS hp
LEFT JOIN superpower ON hp.power_id = superpower.id

params.description: Lists each hero's assigned powers with the power name — one row per hero_id × power_id assignment.
params.when_to_use: Get the set of powers (by id and name) assigned to a given hero or set of heroes | Filter heroes by possession of a specific power (by id or name) when building larger hero-level queries | Compose hero-level aggregates that need to account for power assignments (after appropriate re-aggregation) | Join power names onto hero-centric records when you need the textual power label for each assignment
params.output_schema: hero_id: the hero identifier for the assignment — derived from hero_power.hero_id | power_id: the power identifier for the assignment — derived from hero_power.power_id | power_name: the human-readable name of the power — derived from superpower.power_name (via LEFT JOIN on superpower.id = hero_power.power_id)
params.metric: Row-level assignment (no aggregated metrics): each output row represents the existence of an assignment where derived_metric: assignment_exists = 1 for (hero_id, power_id) when a row exists in hero_power | If counting assignments externally: assignment_count(hero_id) = COUNT(hero_power.power_id) grouped by hero_power.hero_id (this COUNT is not performed in this view; examples provided for composition only)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to hero_base on hero_id — safe because hero_base is one-row-per-hero and joining will attach hero attributes to each (hero_id, power_id) assignment without duplicating assignment rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to hero_demographics on hero_id — safe because hero_demographics is also one-row-per-hero (JOIN will not multiply assignment rows). | DO NOT directly join this view to one-to-many tables/views keyed by hero_id (for example hero_attribute_values or any per-hero multi-row detail) without re-aggregation, because those joins would multiply the (hero_id, power_id) assignment rows and thus duplicate counts/measures that assume one row per assignment. | If you need to combine with hero_attribute_values (which is one-to-many per hero), first aggregate that sibling view to one row per hero (e.g., attribute summary or counts) and then join on hero_id — that preserves cardinality. | When composing with hero_power_counts (an aggregate per hero), join on hero_id — safe because hero_power_counts is one-row-per-hero and will not duplicate this view's assignment rows; be mindful that hero_power_counts likely contains aggregated counts of this view's rows. | When composing with hero_power_rank (a ranking over powers per hero) join on (hero_id, power_id) — safe if hero_power_rank is defined one-row-per(hero_id, power_id). | When composing with heroes_with_attributes_and_powers (a JOIN sibling), verify its grain: joining two multi-row-per-hero sources can duplicate rows; only join if that view's grain is compatible (e.g., also hero_id × power_id). | General rule: this view's grain is (hero_id, power_id). Any join on exactly that key (or to a one-row-per-hero table when matching on hero_id) is safe. Joining to tables with many rows per hero or per (hero_id, power_id) requires aggregating those tables first to a compatible grain to avoid accidental duplication.

views.description: One row per hero-power assignment including the superpower name. Useful for counting powers per hero or listing heroes who have a given power. | Use for: List powers for a given hero; Count number of powers per hero; Find heroes who have a specific power_name
validated_on: What are the names of the superheroes with the power of death touch?
What is the average weight of all female superheroes?

views.name: hero_power_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  hp.hero_id,
  COUNT(*) AS power_count
FROM hero_power AS hp
GROUP BY hp.hero_id

params.description: Counts of power assignments per hero (one row per hero_id with the number of hero_power rows for that hero).
params.when_to_use: Get how many powers each hero has (single-hero or multi-hero aggregation). | Join hero power counts as a metric to hero-level dimensional data (e.g., hero name, demographics) without duplicating counts. | Compute derived metrics at the hero grain (e.g., average powers per demographic group) by aggregating the power_count column. | Filter or rank heroes by number of powers before further composition (e.g., select heroes with power_count > N).
params.output_schema: hero_id: identifier of the hero; originates from hero_power.hero_id (grouping key). | power_count: integer count of hero_power rows for that hero; derived from COUNT(*) over hero_power rows for the hero.
params.metric: power_count = COUNT(*) over rows in hero_power grouped by hero_power.hero_id (i.e., number of hero_power records per hero).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to hero_base (NORM) on hero_base.hero_id = hero_id — safe because hero_base is one-row-per-hero so this view's measures are NOT duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to hero_demographics (JOIN) on hero_demographics.hero_id = hero_id — safe if hero_demographics is one-row-per-hero (a hero-level dimension), because hero_power_counts is one-row-per-hero and will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to heroes_with_attributes_and_powers (JOIN) on hero_id = hero_id only if that sibling view is also one-row-per-hero; otherwise treat it as potentially one-to-many and prefer joining to a hero-level projection. | do NOT join directly to hero_power (the base table) without re-aggregating because hero_power is one-to-many to hero_id and joining will multiply power_count (it would reintroduce the many rows that were aggregated away). If you must include power-level detail after joining, first join to hero_power_counts and then separately join hero_power for detail, or re-aggregate after the join. | do NOT join to one-to-many children such as hero_attribute_values (AGG?) or other tables that are multi-row per hero without re-aggregation — joining a one-row-per-hero aggregate to a many-row-per-hero table will multiply the aggregate unless you re-aggregate the result back to hero grain. | If composing further aggregates (e.g., average powers per demographic group), aggregate the power_count column after joining to the dimension: e.g., GROUP BY demographic_key; AVG(power_count) or SUM(power_count) as appropriate. This preserves correctness because power_count is already at hero grain. | When joining to sibling AGG views: safe if the sibling view's grain is the same hero_id (one-row-per-hero). If a sibling AGG view has the same grain, join on hero_id is safe and will not duplicate measures. If the sibling view has a different grain (e.g., per hero_power or per attribute), do not join directly without aligning grains (re-aggregate to hero).

views.description: Aggregated counts of powers per hero (one row per hero). Exposes power_count so downstream queries can filter top-N or join counts to hero details. | Use for: Rank heroes by number of powers; Filter heroes who have at least one power (power_count > 0); Compute distributions of power_count by publisher or alignment

views.name: hero_attribute_summary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ha.hero_id,
  COUNT(ha.attribute_value) AS attribute_count,
  AVG(ha.attribute_value) AS attribute_mean,
  MIN(ha.attribute_value) AS attribute_min,
  MAX(ha.attribute_value) AS attribute_max,
  SUM(ha.attribute_value) AS attribute_sum
FROM hero_attribute AS ha
GROUP BY ha.hero_id

params.description: Per-hero aggregated summary of numeric attribute values: count, mean, min, max, and sum of attribute_value for each hero_id.
params.when_to_use: Get per-hero statistics of attribute_value (counts, average, min, max, sum). | Compose into larger hero-level reports that need attribute aggregates as hero-level metrics. | Filter or rank heroes by attribute_count, attribute_mean, attribute_sum, attribute_min, or attribute_max. | Join with hero-level dimension data (e.g., hero_base, hero_demographics) to enrich hero records without duplicating metrics.
params.output_schema: hero_id: unique identifier of the hero at the view grain; derived from hero_attribute.hero_id (group key). | attribute_count: count of non-null attribute_value for the hero; derived from COUNT(hero_attribute.attribute_value). | attribute_mean: arithmetic average of attribute_value for the hero; derived from AVG(hero_attribute.attribute_value). | attribute_min: minimum observed attribute_value for the hero; derived from MIN(hero_attribute.attribute_value). | attribute_max: maximum observed attribute_value for the hero; derived from MAX(hero_attribute.attribute_value). | attribute_sum: sum of attribute_value for the hero; derived from SUM(hero_attribute.attribute_value).
params.metric: attribute_count = COUNT(hero_attribute.attribute_value) -- counts non-null attribute_value per hero_id | attribute_mean = AVG(hero_attribute.attribute_value) -- mean of attribute_value per hero_id | attribute_min = MIN(hero_attribute.attribute_value) -- minimum attribute_value per hero_id | attribute_max = MAX(hero_attribute.attribute_value) -- maximum attribute_value per hero_id | attribute_sum = SUM(hero_attribute.attribute_value) -- sum of attribute_value per hero_id
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to hero-level dimension views on hero_id (examples: hero_base, hero_demographics) — safe because hero_attribute_summary is aggregated to one row per hero_id, so joining one-to-one or one-to-zero hero dimension rows will not duplicate these measures. | Do NOT join hero_attribute_summary directly to any table or view that is one-to-many from hero_id (for example, hero_attribute (raw rows), hero_power_assignments if a hero can have multiple powers, or heroes_with_attributes_and_powers if it expands heroes into multiple rows) without re-aggregation — doing so will multiply the aggregated measures and produce incorrect totals/averages. | If you must combine with a one-to-many relation (e.g., hero_power_assignments or hero_attribute raw rows), either: (a) join first to a hero-level aggregation of that relation (e.g., hero_power_counts or another AGG on hero_power_assignments) so both sides are one-row-per-hero, or (b) join on hero_id and then re-aggregate the combined result at hero_id (or at a different desired grain) to avoid double-counting. | Safe composition examples: JOIN hero_attribute_summary hs ON hs.hero_id = hero_base.hero_id; JOIN hero_attribute_summary hs ON hs.hero_id = hero_demographics.hero_id; JOIN hero_attribute_summary hs ON hs.hero_id = hero_power_counts.hero_id — all safe because right-hand sides are one-row-per-hero. | Unsafe composition examples: JOIN hero_attribute_summary hs ON hs.hero_id = hero_attribute.hero_id (raw) — unsafe because hero_attribute is multi-row per hero; JOIN hero_attribute_summary hs ON hs.hero_id = hero_power_assignments.hero_id if assignments are multi-valued per hero — unsafe unless you aggregate assignments first.

views.description: Summary statistics per hero across their attributes: attribute_count, attribute_mean, attribute_min, attribute_max, attribute_sum. Use to compare overall attribute profiles between heroes. | Use for: Compare heroes by average attribute value; Filter heroes with many or few measured attributes; Combine attribute summary with hero demographics to find patterns

views.name: hero_power_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  pc.hero_id,
  pc.power_count,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY pc.power_count DESC) AS power_count_rank,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY pc.power_count DESC) AS power_count_row_num
FROM (
  SELECT
    hp.hero_id,
    COUNT(*) AS power_count
  FROM hero_power AS hp
  GROUP BY hp.hero_id
) AS pc

params.description: Ranks heroes by how many powers they have (one row per hero with power count and rank information).
params.when_to_use: Find the heroes with the most/fewest powers (top N, bottom N). | Produce a ranked list of heroes by power_count for reporting or leaderboards. | Compose with hero detail views to show hero attributes alongside their power rank. | Filter or paginate heroes by rank or row number for dashboards.
params.output_schema: hero_id: unique identifier of the hero — derived from hero_power.hero_id (grouping key) | power_count: number of power assignments for the hero — derived from COUNT(*) over hero_power rows in the subquery (alias pc.power_count) | power_count_rank: dense ordering rank of heroes by power_count (ties receive same rank) — defined as RANK() OVER (ORDER BY pc.power_count DESC) | power_count_row_num: row number ordering of heroes by power_count (ties get distinct row numbers) — defined as ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY pc.power_count DESC)
params.metric: power_count = COUNT(*) aggregated over hero_power rows grouped by hero_id | power_count_rank = RANK() OVER (ORDER BY power_count DESC) — a window function computed over the set of heroes and their power_count | power_count_row_num = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY power_count DESC) — a window function assigning a unique row position per hero ordered by power_count
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to hero_base (or any one-row-per-hero dimension/view) on hero_id — safe because hero_power_rank is one-row-per-hero so measures (power_count, ranks) will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to hero_demographics on hero_id — safe for the same reason: demographics are one-row-per-hero and will not multiply power_count. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to heroes_with_attributes_and_powers only if that view is known to be one-row-per-hero; verify its grain before joining. If it is one-row-per-hero, join on hero_id is safe. | unsafe-to-join without re-aggregation: do NOT directly join to hero_power (or any raw hero_power_assignments style table/view that is one-to-many to hero_id) on hero_id because those joins will multiply this view's power_count measures (each power row would duplicate the hero row). If you must combine with one-to-many data, either (a) aggregate the other side to one-row-per-hero first, or (b) join then re-aggregate preserving correct measures. | unsafe-to-join without care: do NOT join to hero_attribute_values (or other attribute-value tables that are many-to-many / multi-valued per hero) unless you first reduce them to one-row-per-hero (for example, summarizing or pivoting) because otherwise power_count will be inflated by attribute rows. | planner guidance: when composing additional metrics from joined tables, prefer joins to views known to be at the hero_id grain. If joining multiple one-to-many dimensions, join each separately after aggregating to hero-level and then join the resulting hero-level datasets to hero_power_rank to avoid row multiplication.

views.description: Rank heroes by number of powers (dense rank and row_number available). Useful for top-N hero selection by power_count without baking a limit. | Use for: Select top-N heroes by number of powers (WHERE power_count_rank <= K); Break ties using row number or present dense ranks; Join rank to hero details to show leaders

views.name: heroes_with_attributes_and_powers
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  hb.id AS id,
  hb.superhero_name AS superhero_name,
  hb.full_name AS full_name,
  hb.gender_id AS gender_id,
  hb.eye_colour_id AS eye_colour_id,
  hb.hair_colour_id AS hair_colour_id,
  hb.skin_colour_id AS skin_colour_id,
  hb.race_id AS race_id,
  hb.publisher_id AS publisher_id,
  hb.alignment_id AS alignment_id,
  ha.attribute_id AS attribute_id,
  attribute.attribute_name AS attribute_name,
  ha.attribute_value AS attribute_value,
  COALESCE(pc.power_count, 0) AS power_count,
  hb.height_cm AS height_cm,
  hb.weight_kg AS weight_kg
FROM superhero AS hb
LEFT JOIN hero_attribute AS ha ON hb.id = ha.hero_id
LEFT JOIN attribute ON ha.attribute_id = attribute.id
LEFT JOIN (

params.description: Provides one row per (hero id, attribute) with hero identifying info, the attribute name/value, the hero's power count, and basic physical/demographic columns.
params.when_to_use: List hero attributes along with hero-level metrics (e.g., how many powers a hero has) when you need attribute-level rows (one row per hero-attribute). | Drill-down queries that filter or group by attribute_id or attribute_name while keeping hero details and power_count available. | Composing further aggregations over attributes (for example: count of heroes by attribute_value) while preserving an accurate per-hero power_count when aggregated correctly.
params.output_schema: id: hero id (source: superhero.id) — the primary identifier of the hero; grain includes id so each row is tied to this hero. | superhero_name: hero display name (source: superhero.superhero_name). | full_name: hero real/full name (source: superhero.full_name). | gender_id: foreign key to gender reference (source: superhero.gender_id). | eye_colour_id: foreign key to eye colour (source: superhero.eye_colour_id). | hair_colour_id: foreign key to hair colour (source: superhero.hair_colour_id). | skin_colour_id: foreign key to skin colour (source: superhero.skin_colour_id). | race_id: foreign key to race (source: superhero.race_id). | publisher_id: foreign key to publisher (source: superhero.publisher_id). | alignment_id: foreign key to alignment (source: superhero.alignment_id). | attribute_id: attribute identifier for this row (source: hero_attribute.attribute_id). | attribute_name: human name for the attribute (source: attribute.attribute_name). | attribute_value: the hero's value for this attribute (source: hero_attribute.attribute_value). | power_count: derived metric — number of powers assigned to this hero (derived from aggregate on hero_power.hero_id). | height_cm: hero height in cm (source: superhero.height_cm). | weight_kg: hero weight in kg (source: superhero.weight_kg).
params.grounded_columns: superhero.id | superhero.superhero_name | superhero.full_name | superhero.gender_id | superhero.eye_colour_id | superhero.hair_colour_id | superhero.skin_colour_id | superhero.race_id | superhero.publisher_id | superhero.alignment_id | hero_attribute.hero_id | hero_attribute.attribute_id | hero_attribute.attribute_value | attribute.id | attribute.attribute_name | hero_power.hero_id | hero_power (used in aggregate COUNT(*)) | superhero.height_cm | superhero.weight_kg
params.metric: power_count = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hero_power hp WHERE hp.hero_id = superhero.id)  -- implemented as an aggregated subquery aliased pc.power_count then COALESCE(pc.power_count, 0)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to publisher, gender, race, alignment, eye_colour, hair_colour, skin_colour, attribute (dimension/detail tables) on their id keys — safe because these are one-to-one (or many-to-one from this view to the dimension) and will not duplicate this view's rows or its power_count measure. | Safe: Join to attribute (or attribute lookup views) on attribute_id = attribute.id — the view already LEFT JOINs attribute and preserves one row per hero-attribute; joining attribute again by id will not multiply measures. | Safe: Join to hero_demographics (one-row-per-hero normalized view) on id = hero_demographics.id — safe because hero_demographics is one-row-per-hero and this view is at most one row per (hero, attribute), so it will not multiply hero-level aggregates beyond the attribute granularity. | Do NOT join this view directly to any table or view that is one-to-many from hero (for example hero_power, hero_power_assignments, or any raw power assignment table) without first aggregating that table to one row per hero. Joining a raw hero_power (many rows per hero) will duplicate rows for heroes that have multiple powers and thus will multiply power_count and any hero-level metrics in this view. | Do NOT join to hero_attribute (raw) again on hero_id without aggregating or deduplicating, because this view already exposes hero_attribute rows; re-joining the raw hero_attribute will create many-to-many duplication when attribute-level detail is also present. | If you need to combine this view with another one-to-many detail (e.g., power assignments) and produce correct hero-level aggregates, either: a) aggregate the one-to-many side to hero_id first (e.g., count, sum) and then join on hero_id, or b) start from a purely hero-level view (hero_base or hero_demographics) and join both attribute and power details in controlled aggregations. | Explanation of why power_count is not duplicated by safe joins: power_count is pre-aggregated to one row per hero in the inline subquery (pc) and then left-joined by hero id. Joining additional one-row-per-hero dimensions preserves that cardinality. Only joining additional many-rows-per-hero sources will duplicate rows and therefore would multiply measures unless those sources are aggregated to hero level first.
